title: Lesson file, format 1.9
description: One file per lesson. The lesson page, the teacher page, the Word student sheets and teacher notes, the how-to links, the AI assistant's knowledge entry and the AI prompt are made from it. The Atlas app, Hub, assistant, licence and product names come from the lessons settings file (<name>-lessons.json), not from the lesson. Text fields allow **bold** and [link text](https://address) only.

byLang.description: Text in each language listed under languages.

tool.description: A key from tools in site.json, such as bookmarks, popups or measure. The checker confirms it exists, so the list lives in one place.

contentVersion.description: Bump on every change: patch for typos, minor for new or changed questions, major for a new map.

status.description: For the team's own tracking. Not shown on the pages.

subject.description: Should match a key in hub.subjectPaths in site.json.

course.description: Should match a key in hub.coursePaths in site.json.

unit.description: One of the units listed for the course in site.json (units). The Lessons page is grouped and ordered by that list.

alsoFits.description: Optional. Other units from the course's list that this lesson also serves.

subjects.description: Subjects the lesson serves, the course's own first (US History, Geography, Civics…).

about.description: Two to four sentences about the map as a whole: the place and period it covers, its main layers and which are off when it opens. Shown first under About this map on the lesson page, which can be shared with students, so no answers and no questions.

bookmarks.description: Bookmark names exactly as in the map. Vera uses them, so list every one.

preview.description: True when the picture is a stand-in (the item thumbnail) rather than a screenshot of the map as it opens.

image.description: Optional picture of the map: an https URL with alt text. Best is a screenshot of the map as it opens, about 1200 x 675, in resources/assets/screenshots on GitHub Pages; preview: true marks a stand-in such as the web map item's thumbnail.

where.description: Layer, question or sheet the issue affects.

steps.description: What the student does on the map, one action per step, in order: open, click, turn on, zoom, measure, read. No questions here.

ask.description: The question(s) the student answers in writing, after the steps.

fill.description: Optional fill-in line. Use ________ for the blank.

lines.description: Optional. Writing lines under this question on the student sheet. Default 2 on a one-page sheet, 3 on a two-page sheet (a lesson with studentSupport).

where.description: Where on the map a student finds it: the layer, bookmark, pop-up field or tool, and the value to expect. For example: Lexington and Concord pop-up, Dates field; Measure tool, Boston to Concord, about 16 miles (accept 15 to 17).

accept.description: For reasoning questions: what a good answer includes, so a teacher can grade without a model answer.

text.description: Extra notes for the teacher, or the answer itself where a value is needed.

answer.description: Teacher-only. Shown on the lesson's teacher page and in the teacher notes Word file, never on the lesson page, in Vera's file or in the AI prompt. Say where on the map the answer is found and what to accept; keep bare answer values for counts and tables.

core.description: True on exactly one question: the one to use if there is only time for one.

minutes.description: About how long this question takes.

frontOfClass.description: Steps for teaching this question from the front: what to open, click or turn on, and what to ask. One action per line.

objectives.description: Learning objectives: 3 to 5 lines completing 'Students will…'.

differentiation.description: One line each: how to support students who find it hard, and how to stretch students who finish.

instructionalModels.description: Optional. Ways to run the lesson; defaults to site.json teaching.instructionalModels.

resources.description: Further reading for teachers, National Geographic Education first where a resource exists.

assessment.description: Format 1.7. Assessing the answer to the compelling question, for teachers (English). The shared four-level rubric lives in site.json rubric; this block adds the lesson's own line about map evidence and a model answer. Never shown to students or to Vera.

evidence.description: One or two sentences: the layers, features, dates, numbers or distances a strong answer draws on in this lesson.

exemplar.description: A model answer at the top level of the rubric, about 80 to 200 words, written as a strong grade 8 student would, naming where on the map each piece of evidence comes from.

studentSupport.description: Optional. Extra help on the student sheet. A lesson with it gets a two-page sheet with section headings and more room to write.

beforeYouStart.description: Two or three sentences of context, so a student who missed the lesson can begin. Don't give away answers.

readingTheMap.description: What the map's symbols mean, in plain words, checked against the web map.

tips.description: Keys of tips in site.json sheetText.<language>.tips, such as popups.

reflection.description: A closing question for students to look back on what the map showed them.

licence.description: Only when this lesson's licence differs from the one in the lessons settings file. Leave it out otherwise.
